Chapter 9: Healing and Forgiveness—The Other Side of Justice
When you hear the word "justice," what comes to mind? For a lot of people, it’s punishment, retribution—making sure someone pays for what they’ve done. But for many, real healing takes root somewhere else. Forgiveness—whether you’re the one giving it, or the one receiving it—can transform everything. It’s a way forward, especially when anger and pain threaten to take over.
Let me share a story. There was a father whose world shattered when his daughter was killed in a senseless act of violence. For years, he was lost—grief and rage eating away at him, keeping him stuck in the past. But then, something remarkable happened. He met the young man responsible. At first, their conversation was awkward, heavy with sadness. But as they kept talking, honesty began to break through. The father stopped seeing a monster and recognized a scared, broken person in front of him.
Over time, he found a way to forgive. Not because he excused what happened—far from it. But because he refused to let that one terrible moment define his life forever.
There’s another story too—a woman who was wrongfully convicted. She spent years battling to clear her name, her anger toward the system growing with every setback. When she was finally exonerated, she had a choice: stay bitter, or move on. She chose the latter. Instead of holding on to her anger, she spoke out, sharing her experience so others might avoid the same fate. Her forgiveness wasn’t really for the people who wronged her—it was for herself. It was how she took her life back.
Most people don’t think about forgiveness when they imagine justice. It seems like something private, tucked away from the rules and judgments of the law. But here’s something important—healing and forgiveness are essential if we want justice to be truly just. They let people move beyond the past, rebuild relationships, and even find meaning in their suffering.
What really becomes clear is this: justice isn’t just about what happens inside a courtroom. It’s also about what happens inside our hearts and minds—in those quiet moments when someone chooses to let go of their anger and reach for compassion instead.
These stories of healing and forgiveness remind us: justice isn’t only about punishment. It’s about restoration. It’s about making things right—not just for victims, but for everyone touched by crime.
